# Canadian Wood-Frame House Construction — Chapters 11 & 12 — Extracted Notes

**Source:** *Canadian Wood-Frame House Construction*, Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC / SCHL). Chapter 11 "Ceiling and Roof Framing" (pp. 118–135) and Chapter 12 "Roof Sheathing and Coverings" (pp. 136–147). Figures 77–106. Extracted from `Canadian Wood-Frame House Construction - Chapters 11-12.pdf`.

**Scope of source:** Site-built and trussed pitched roofs (gable, hip, valley, dormer, gable-end projections), low-slope roofs, roof space ventilation, worked sizing examples, roof sheathing (panel and board), eave protection, and roof coverings (asphalt shingles, wood shingles, shakes, built-up, sheet metal, tile). Metric with imperial in brackets; lumber sizes are actual dressed sizes (38 × 89 mm = 2 × 4 in. nominal). Span/nailing tables referenced (Tables 19–38) are **not** included in this excerpt.

---

## Contents of the source document

**Chapter 11 — Ceiling and Roof Framing**
- Roof slope conventions
- Pitched Roofs · Prefabricated Roof Trusses · Site Assembly of Pitched Roofs
- Gable-End Framing and Projections
- Low-Slope Roofs
- Roof Space Ventilation
- Worked examples: Choosing the size and spacing of Ceiling Joists / Roof Rafters / Roof Joists
- Sustainable Housing Insight

**Chapter 12 — Roof Sheathing and Coverings**
- Roof Sheathing · Installing Roof Sheathing · Roof Sheathing Details
- Eave Protection
- Roof Coverings: Asphalt Shingles (≥1:3 and 1:6–1:3) · Wood Shingles · Shakes · Finish at Ridge and Hips · Built-up Roofs · Sheet Metal Roofing · Concrete and Clay Tile Roofing
- Sustainable Housing Insight

---

## Key dimensions quick reference

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Truss / rafter / joist spacing | generally 600 mm (24 in.) o.c.; also 400 mm (16 in.), 300 mm (12 in.) |
| Metric "soft" spacings vs actual panel-fit spacings | 300/400/600 mm nominal → 305/406/610 mm actual to suit 1220 × 2440 mm (4 × 8 ft) panels |
| Heel depth at outer face of exterior wall (insulation) | ≥ 300 mm (12 in.) |
| Hip and valley rafters | ~50 mm (2 in.) deeper than common / jack rafters |
| Ridge beam for slope < 1:3 | 38 × 140 mm (2 × 6) supported at 1.2 m (4 ft) intervals by 38 × 89 mm (2 × 4) struts |
| Collar ties (slope ≥ 1:3) | 38 × 89 mm (2 × 4); if > 2.4 m (8 ft) long, brace with 19 × 89 mm (1 × 4) continuous member, three 76 mm (3 in.) nails each end |
| Struts | 38 × 89 mm (2 × 4), angle ≥ 45° from horizontal |
| Strongback (hip end support) | two 38 × 89 mm nailed together on edge, struts 38 × 89 mm |
| Knee/dwarf wall struts | 1.2 m (4 ft) o.c. |
| Beam under dwarf wall | underside raised ≥ 25 mm (1 in.) above ceiling finish |
| Rafter plate nails | ≥ two 100 mm (4 in.) nails per ceiling joist |
| Gable-end stud nails | ≥ four 63 mm (2½ in.) nails each end |
| Gable overhang < 300 mm (12 in.) | rake rafter + 19 mm (¾ in.) nailing strip + blocking 600 mm o.c. |
| Gable overhang > 300 mm (12 in.) | lookouts, same size as rafters, 600 mm (24 in.) o.c., length ≥ 2 × overhang; double rafter if lookouts project > 1.5 rafter spaces |
| Low-slope roof minimum drainage slope | 1:50 |
| Low-slope lookouts | header of two joists if projecting > 1.5 joist spaces |
| Ventilation clearance above insulation | ≥ 63 mm (2½ in.) without baffles; 25 mm (1 in.) with baffles |
| Cross-purlins over roof-ceiling joists (low slope) | 38 × 64 mm (2 × 3) |
| Vent area, slope ≥ 1:6 | ≥ 1/300 of insulated ceiling area |
| Vent area, slope < 1:6 | ≥ 1/150 of ceiling area |
| Vent distribution | ≥ 25% at bottom (eaves), ≥ 25% at top |
| Attic access hatch | ≥ 0.32 m² (3.4 sq ft), no dimension < 500 mm (20 in.) |
| Permanent truss bracing repeat | ~6 m (20 ft) intervals; 38 × 89 mm web bracing |
| Trusses installed by hand | span < 6 m (20 ft) |
| Panel sheathing gap | 2–3 mm (⅛ in.) between sheets |
| Panel sheathing nailing | 150 mm (6 in.) o.c. edges, 300 mm (12 in.) o.c. intermediate |
| Blocking under unsupported panel edges | 38 × 38 mm (2 × 2) or metal H-clips |
| Staples for 9.5 mm sheathing | 1.6 mm thick, 38.1 mm long, 9.5 mm crown, crown parallel to framing |
| Min sheathing for built-up walking deck | 15.5 mm (⅝ in.) |
| Board sheathing thickness | 19 mm (¾ in. nominal); 17 mm (11/16 in.) if supports ≤ 400 mm o.c. |
| Board sheathing nails | ≤ 184 mm wide: two 51 mm nails per bearing; > 184 mm: three; high wind: 63 mm nails |
| Board sheathing max width | 286 mm (12 in. nominal) |
| Spaced board sheathing (wood shingles/shakes) | boards on centres = shingle exposure; 19 × 89 mm strips for shakes, never > 250 mm |
| Chimney clearance (sheathing & framing) | 50 mm (2 in.) interior; 12 mm (½ in.) exterior masonry |
| Eave protection extent | ≥ 900 mm (36 in.) up slope, to ≥ 300 mm (12 in.) inside inner face of exterior wall |
| Eave protection not required | unheated garages/porches; slope ≥ 1:1.5; ≤ 3,500 heating degree-days |
| Roll roofing laps (eave protection) | ≥ 100 mm (4 in.), cemented |
| Min slope — asphalt shingles (low-slope application) | 1:6 |
| Min slope — wood shingles | 1:4 |
| Min slope — shakes / asphalt shingles (normal application) | 1:3 |
| Min slope — sheet metal | 1:4 |
| Asphalt strip shingle | 310 × 915 mm (12 × 36 in.) or 335 × 1000 mm; 3 tabs; exposure 130 mm (5 in.) or 145 mm (5¾ in.); 21–26 strips/bundle ≈ 3 m² |
| Starter strip projection | ≥ 12 mm (½ in.) beyond eaves/rakes/fascia; nailed 300 mm o.c. |
| Asphalt shingle nails | four large-head roofing nails per strip, penetrating ≥ 12 mm into sheathing |
| Low-slope asphalt (1:6–1:3) | three thicknesses; exposure ≤ ⅓ shingle height; cement bands 200 mm (starter), exposure + 100 mm (first course), exposure + 50 mm (subsequent), band 25–50 mm above butt; cold cement 0.5 L/m², hot 1 kg/m² |
| Wood shingles | width 75–350 mm (3–14 in.); No. 1/No. 2 grade; western red / white cedar |
| Wood shingle laying | first course doubled, projects ~25 mm (1 in.) past fascia; 6 mm (¼ in.) gap; joint offset ≥ 40 mm over 2 previous courses; two nails per shingle at exposure + 40 mm from butt, 20 mm edge distance |
| Shakes | length ≥ 450 mm (18 in.); width 100–350 mm; butt 9–32 mm; exposure 190 mm for 450 mm shakes, 250 mm for 600 mm shakes |
| Shake laying | 900 mm No. 15 felt at eave; starter doubled (or tripled); 450 mm felt strip over top of each course, bottom edge at 2 × exposure above butt; gap 6–9 mm; side joint offset ≥ 40 mm |
| Ridge/hip cap (wood) | 150 mm (6 in.) wide shingles alternately lapped, blind-nailed |
| Built-up roof at wall | turned up ≥ 150 mm (6 in.); counter-flashing into mortar ≥ 25 mm, down ~150 mm, lap ≥ 100 mm; 50 mm min lap membrane flashing |
| Sheet metal widths | 762–914 mm (30–36 in.) |
| Sheet metal min thickness | 0.33 mm galvanized steel; 0.46 mm copper/zinc; 0.48 mm aluminum |
| Roof surface dimensions (waste reduction) | multiples of 400 or 600 mm (16 or 24 in.) |

---

## Roof slope conventions (p. 118–119)

- Slope = rise-to-run ratio, **rise always first**. Two conventions:
  - **Imperial:** run always 12 (framing square). 45° = 12/12; 4/12 = 4 in. rise per 12 in. run.
  - **Ratio:** for slopes < 45° the *first* number (vertical) is 1 (e.g. 1:5 = 1 vertical per 5 horizontal); for slopes > 45° the *second* number (horizontal) is 1 (e.g. 5:1). Avoid mixed units (1 mm in 10 m).
  - 4/12 ≡ 1:3. Angular expressions acceptable where high accuracy needed.
- Pitched roofs vary from **1:6 to 1:1 or more**. Minimum slope for asphalt shingles is 1:6; different installation rules for ≥ 1:3 and < 1:3.
- Roof must have water-shedding surface, air and vapour barriers, thermal insulation and ventilation. Most Canadian houses: prefabricated trusses + unheated ventilated attic. Cathedral ceilings and flat roofs still need a vented space above insulation.
- Roof joist/rafter sizes by species/grade/live load: Tables 29–32 (pp. 295–301, not in excerpt).

---

## Chapter 11 — Ceiling and Roof Framing

### Pitched roofs (p. 119)
- Prefabricated trusses most often used; site-framed rafters sometimes. **Gable roof is simplest**; hip or L-shape roofs can also be trussed (**Fig. 77**: L-shape trussed roof — plan with hatched roof planes and a valley; isometric shows ridge, valley trusses, roof sheathing, gable end, girder truss, common trusses, double wall plates).

### Prefabricated roof trusses (pp. 119–122)
- Advantages: designed for local snow loads, quality control, less lumber waste, faster enclosure; provide surface for sheathing and ceiling, space for insulation.
- **Raised heel trusses** (**Fig. 78**) used in most new houses — deeper space at the eaves for insulation; truss anchors as requested by manufacturer/code. Energy codes lead to vertical depth ≥ 300 mm (12 in.) at outer face of exterior wall for trusses, rafters and roof joists.
- Trusses typically span exterior wall to exterior wall, no intermediate bearing → partitions placed freely; continuous air barrier/vapour retarder applied to underside before partitions.
- **Fig. 79 — Types of prefabricated roof trusses:** king-post · Howe · Fink or W · mono-pitch · parallel chord · scissor truss · mansard.
- Storage flat and clean; spans < 6 m (20 ft) installed by hand, longer need lifting equipment. Lift vertically to avoid lateral bending.
- Erection: gable truss first, braced to ground and wall; each additional truss generally **600 mm (24 in.) o.c.**, toe-nailed to top plates, temporarily braced (**Fig. 80** — gable ends normally sheathed before end braces). Then permanent bracing (**Fig. 81**): (a) top chord plane, (b) lateral web bracing, (c) web/bottom chord plane. Plan view: lateral braces across top chords, diagonal brace nailed to web repeated at ~6 m (20 ft); end elevation: 38 × 89 mm web bracing; side elevation: sheathing, blocking, lateral brace, diagonal braced bay at both ends and ~6 m intervals. Sheathing adds stiffness. Do not cut or alter trusses.

### Site assembly of pitched roofs (pp. 122–127)

**Fig. 82 — Types of pitched roofs:** Flat · Monopitch · Gable · Hip · Gambrel · Mansard.

- Gable roof: rafters/trusses same length and pattern. Dormers add light/headroom (Fig. 88). **Hip roof: common rafters fastened to a ridge board, hip rafters supporting the jack rafters (Fig. 83B).**
- Liveable attics need insulation, air barrier, vapour barrier; framing may need to be upsized for insulation depth.
- **Ceiling joists** support ceiling finish and act as ties between exterior walls / opposing rafters; may carry loads from dwarf (knee) walls → size accordingly (Table 33); if they carry floor loads use floor joist tables (Tables 19, 20).
- Nail ceiling joists **after wall framing, before rafters** (rafter thrust otherwise pushes walls out). Joists tie lower ends of rafters in roofs sloping **≥ 1:3**; nail ceiling joist to side of each pair of rafters (**Fig. 83**).
- **Hip roofs:** where jack rafters run perpendicular to ceiling joists, a **stub joist** ties the jack rafter back to the ceiling joist (**Fig. 85**). Lap and nail joists or splice at centre bearing wall for a continuous tie. Nail counts depend on slope, spacing, snow load, house width (Table 24).

**Fig. 83 — Roof framing and attachment**
- **A Gable roof:** ridge board, rafter, collar brace, collar tie, gable end stud, ceiling joist, top wall plate.
- **B Hip roof:** hip rafter **at least 50 mm (2 in.) deeper than jack rafters**, jack rafter, ceiling joist, top plate. Isometric: four hip rafters rising from the corners to a short ridge (shown as a vertical post marker at the apex in the drawing), jack rafters from plates to hips, common rafters from plates to ridge, ceiling joists spanning the short direction.

- Dwarf walls perpendicular to ceiling joists (**Fig. 84**) add roof load; increase joist depth one size when slope > 1:4; when ≤ 1:4 use roof joist tables.
- **Fig. 84 — Rafter heel supported on a rafter plate:** rafter plate nailed to top of each ceiling joist with ≥ two 100 mm (4 in.) nails; rafter; ridge beam; exterior wall; knee wall with top and bottom plates and stud in line with each ceiling joist and rafter; struts at 1.2 m (4 ft) o.c.; ceiling joists lapped directly above interior load-bearing wall.
- Hip rafters ~51 mm (2 in.) deeper than common/jack rafters reduce space along end walls; in low-slope roofs the outside ceiling joist may not fit at normal spacing → **doubled joists** positioned to suit, then **tail joists** toenailed to outside wall plate and end-nailed to the doubled joist, at the same spacing as main joists (**Fig. 85**: jack rafter, hip rafter ≥ 50 mm deeper, ceiling joist, double ceiling joist, normal location for ceiling joist if space available, stub joist, end wall framing top plate).
- **Cutting rafters:** proper angle at ridge; **bird's mouth** notches at eaves; heel bears directly over exterior wall. Rafters placed: (a) directly on wall plates (Fig. 83); (b) on a rafter plate on the ceiling joists (Fig. 84); (c) on a load-bearing wall supported on the exterior wall plate (**Fig. 86**, used where part of the outside wall is inset — ceiling joists extend beyond exterior wall and are nailed to rafter sides).
- **Ridge board or ridge beam** ensures a level ridgeline. Erect rafters in pairs, nail to ridge, toe-nail lower ends to wall plate. Pairs directly opposite or **offset at ridge by ≤ their thickness** (offset needed when joists are lapped at the centre wall).
- **Slope < 1:3 → vertical support at peak:** 38 × 140 mm (2 × 6) ridge beam supported at 1.2 m (4 ft) by 38 × 89 mm (2 × 4) struts, or a load-bearing wall. Ridge support eliminates outward thrust → continuous ties unnecessary. Ridge beams also needed on steep roofs where rafter ends can't be tied.
- **Intermediate support** between ridge and exterior walls reduces rafter span (span measured from intermediate point to ridge/eave):
  - Slope ≥ 1:3: 38 × 89 mm **collar ties** nailed to each rafter pair; ties > 2.4 m (8 ft) braced against buckling with a 19 × 89 mm continuous member at right angles near centre (three 76 mm nails each end).
  - Slope < 1:3: **dwarf bearing wall** (Fig. 84), single top plate allowed if rafters over studs.
  - **Struts** 38 × 89 mm nailed to rafter side, bearing on load-bearing partition, **≥ 45° from horizontal** (Fig. 86).
  - Rafters perpendicular to ceiling joists: dwarf wall on a **beam between ceiling joists**, beam underside ≥ 25 mm (1 in.) above ceiling finish via blocks at bearing points.
  - Hip/valley rafters: beam with roof strut; or for a few rafters at a hip end a **"strongback"** of two 38 × 89 mm nailed on edge under the rafters, supported by 38 × 89 mm struts radiating from a common point on the interior bearing wall.
- **Hip and valley rafters ~50 mm (2 in.) deeper than common rafters** → full contact with the angle-cut of jack rafters (Figs. 83, 85, 87). Hip roof: jack rafters nailed to hip rafters and wall plate. Valley: jack rafters nailed to valley rafter and ridge.
- **Fig. 86 — Rafter heel supported on load-bearing wall:** ridge board; intermediate struts ≥ 45° to horizontal; 38 mm (2 in.) splice plate; interior bearing wall; rafters notched and bearing on top plate of exterior wall; continuous nailer and soffit supports; ceiling joists extend beyond exterior wall, nailed to rafters and toe-nailed to double wall plate; studs in load-bearing wall directly under each rafter; wall sheathing; exterior wall. Inset shows a house with an inset wall portion.
- **Fig. 87 — Framing at a valley:** valley rafter, jack rafter, common rafter, top plate, corner wall studs (inside corner of an L-plan: valley rafter rises from the inside corner; jack rafters from each wing's plate to the valley).
- **Dormers (Fig. 88):** rafters each side **doubled** to support side studs and valley rafters; top ends of valley rafters on a **double header** between the doubled rafters (joist hangers). Usual method: install roof sheathing first, frame dormer, cut sheathing flush with framing around opening; **bottom plate on top of the sheathing** supports side studs and is nailing base for wall sheathing. Size window for flashing/detailing.

### Gable-end framing and projections (pp. 127–129)
- After roof framing, nail **gable-end studs**; in unfinished attics wide face may be parallel to wall; cut to rafter angle, toenail to plate and rafter underside with ≥ four 63 mm (2½ in.) nails each end.
- **Projection < 300 mm (12 in.)** (**Fig. 90 — Narrow projection**): **rake rafter** supported by ridge beam, rafter header, blocking and sheathing; 19 mm (¾ in.) nailing strip fastened to rafter above gable wall; blocking 600 mm (24 in.) o.c. toenailed to strip, end-nailed to rake rafter; soffit nailed to these, fascia added; gable wall sheathing taken up to underside of roof sheathing; rough fascia supports heel of rake rafter.
- **Projection > 300 mm (12 in.)** (**Fig. 89 — Wide projection supported by "lookout" rafters**): gable-end studs with narrow face parallel to sheathing + top wall plate; **lookouts** same size as rafters, **600 mm (24 in.) o.c.**, end-nailed to the first rafter inboard and to the gable top plate; blocking between lookouts at the wall line supports sheathing and inner soffit edge; **lookout length ≥ 2 × overhang**; **double rafter** where lookouts project > 1.5 rafter spaces into the roof. Labels: ridge beam, rafter, top plate of gable end wall, blocking between lookouts, lookouts 600 mm o.c., ceiling joist, top plate, header or rough fascia, fascia board at eave and gable end, corner studs.

### Low-slope roofs (pp. 129–130)
- Must be more watertight (poorer drainage); may carry decks/traffic → durable materials.
- Rafters doubling as ceiling joists = **"roof joists"**, sized for roof + ceiling loads (Tables 29, 30); may need wider lumber / engineered wood for insulation and ventilation depth.
- Laid level or nearly level; **slope ≥ 1:50 for drainage** via ledger strip on bearing wall or tapered strip on joists.
- Overhang via **lookout rafters** (**Fig. 91**): if projecting > 1.5 joist spaces, two roof joists nailed together form a header; outside rafter header end-nailed to lookouts and joists (nailing for sheathing, fascia, soffit). Labels: alternative framing layout (dashed), roof joist, lookout rafter, header, exterior wall plate, rafter header.

### Roof space ventilation (pp. 130–131)
- Always ventilate above insulation; membranes are vapour-resistant so vapour must be removed by ventilation.
- **Ice dams:** heat loss + sun melts roof snow, refreezes on cold eaves → water backs up (Fig. 100). Airtightness + insulation + ventilation keeps attic cold.
- Clearance between insulation and sheathing: **≥ 63 mm (2½ in.) without baffles, 25 mm (1 in.) with baffles**.
- **Vent area: ≥ 1/300 of insulated ceiling area for slopes ≥ 1:6; ≥ 1/150 for slopes < 1:6**; roof, gable or eave vents (**Fig. 92** soffit ventilation: baffle, perforated soffit, pre-finished fascia, airflow; **Fig. 93** ridge vent and gable vent). Uniformly distributed, ≥ 25% at bottom, ≥ 25% at top.
- Batt insulation between roof-ceiling joists (low slope): ≥ 63 mm vent space — achievable with **38 × 64 mm (2 × 3) cross-purlins** at right angles over joists (may be shimmed for slope). Rigid insulation above sheathing → no ventilation needed.
- Vents must exclude rain, snow, insects; baffle if moisture source; corrosion-resistant metal/plastic screens.
- **Attic access hatch ≥ 0.32 m² (3.4 sq ft), no dimension < 500 mm (20 in.)** except very small attics.

### Worked sizing examples (pp. 132–134)

| Example | Conditions | Selection |
|---|---|---|
| **Ceiling joists (Fig. 94)** | Inaccessible attic, no storage; ceiling carries insulation + drywall; span 4.3 m (14 ft 2 in.); spacing 400 mm (16 in.); SPF No. 2 and better | Table 33 → **38 × 140 mm (2 × 6)** |
| **Roof rafters (Fig. 95)** | Ottawa; snow load 1.72 kPa (36 psf); slope 1:3; rafter span 4.7 m (15 ft 6 in.); SPF No. 2; shingle roofing; lower ends restrained | Table 31 → **38 × 184 mm (2 × 8) at 300 mm o.c.** or **38 × 235 mm (2 × 10) at 600 mm o.c.** |
| **Roof joists (Fig. 96)** | Ottawa; 1.72 kPa; slope 1 in 3; roof joist span 4.19 m (13 ft 9 in.); SPF No. 2; shingles; lower ends restrained | Table 29 → **38 × 235 mm (2 × 10) at 400 mm o.c.** or **38 × 286 mm (2 × 12) at 600 mm o.c.** |

Note (p. 132): National Building Code metric spacings are soft conversions — 12/16/24 in. → 300/400/600 mm; to suit 1220 × 2440 mm (4 × 8 ft) panels actual spacing is commonly **305/406/610 mm** o.c. Members must also be deep enough for required insulation.

### Sustainable housing insight — Ch. 11 (p. 135)
- Energy: raised heel trusses / deep rafters for insulation over exterior walls; consider deeper members or closer spacing for future solar panels.
- Resource: trusses use select lumber + metal plates for long spans, less wood; suit local climate; fast; space for insulation/ventilation; all roof shapes; no site cut-offs.
- Affordability: plan attic conversion — stair location, size ceiling joists as floor joists, movable insulation, steeper slopes shed snow and enclose more attic volume, rough-in services.

---

## Chapter 12 — Roof Sheathing and Coverings

### Roof sheathing (pp. 136–138)
- Sheathing-grade plywood, OSB or lumber planks over trusses/joists/rafters → nailing base for roofing + lateral bracing.
- **Panels (Fig. 97):** face grain **at right angles to framing**, joints offset (staggered), **2–3 mm (⅛ in.) gap**. Nails **150 mm (6 in.) o.c. minimum at edges, 300 mm (12 in.) o.c. intermediate**. Edge support: metal H-clips, 38 × 38 mm (2 × 2) blocking, or tongue-and-groove plywood. Thickness per Table 35 (depends on support spacing and edge support). Stagger fasteners at adjoining panel edges. Staples for 9.5 mm sheathing: 1.6 mm thick, 38.1 mm long, 9.5 mm crown, crown parallel to framing. Built-up roofing used as walking deck needs ≥ 15.5 mm (⅝ in.) sheathing.
- **Lumber boards (Fig. 98):** laid closed (edge to edge), ends supported, joints staggered. High wind/earthquake: laid **diagonally** or engineered. Usually 19 mm (¾ in.) thick; 17 mm allowed when supports ≤ 400 mm o.c. Boards ≤ 184 mm (8 in. nominal) wide: two 51 mm (2 in.) nails per bearing; wider: three; high wind: 63 mm nails. **No boards wider than 286 mm (12 in. nominal).** For wood shingle roofs boards may be **spaced** at the shingle exposure on centre (damp climates; lets shingles dry). Fig. 98 shows spaced method (nailing strips) above and closed method (roof boards, joint) below, on rafters/ceiling joists/plate.
- **Details (Fig. 99):** **50 mm (2 in.) clearance** of sheathing and framing from interior masonry/metal chimneys (12 mm / ½ in. for exterior masonry chimneys); header around opening; nail sheathing to rafters and headers. Fit sheathing tightly at **valleys and hips** and nail to valley/hip rafter → smooth base for flashing. Figure shows L-plan roof with valley, chimney opening with header, rafters, ridge board, ceiling joist, plate, stud.

### Eave protection (pp. 138–140)
- Membrane along roof edge against water entry. **Not required** over unheated garages/porches, slope ≥ 1:1.5, or regions ≤ 3,500 heating degree-days.
- Extends **≥ 900 mm (36 in.) up the roof** (measured along slope) to **≥ 300 mm (12 in.) inside the inner face of the exterior wall** (horizontal). Installed under shingle starter course; usually self-adhering bituminous or roll roofing membrane (type S smooth or type M mineral-surfaced roll roofing, joints lapped ≥ 100 mm and cemented; or peel-and-stick).
- **Fig. 100 — Eave protection:** top: no protection — snow, trapped water backs up through membrane, thin ice slab under snow, melted snow running down underside of sheathing, ice in eavestrough; bottom: protection directs water off the roof. Prevent ice damming by air-sealing ceiling, ceiling/wall junction, penetrations; adequate insulation; eave venting. Keep skylights away from ice-dam areas.

### Roof coverings (pp. 140–146)
- Install as soon as sheathing is on. Asphalt shingles common on pitched roofs; prefinished metal/galvanized steel/aluminum common in some regions (sheds snow); also roll roofing, wood shingles, shakes, sheet metal, concrete/clay tile; built-up with gravel/cap sheet for low slopes. Min/max slopes per covering in Table 36.
- **Minimum slopes: 1:6 asphalt shingles (low-slope application); 1:4 wood shingles; 1:3 hand-split shakes and asphalt shingles (normal application).**

#### Asphalt shingles on slopes ≥ 1:3 (**Fig. 101**)
- Min No. 210 grade; square-butt strip **310 × 915 mm (12 × 36 in.)** or **335 × 1000 mm**, three tabs, exposure **130 mm (5 in.) or 145 mm (5¾ in.)**; 21–26 strips per bundle ≈ 3 m² (32 sq ft). Store flat; distribute bundles on roof.
- Sequence: eave protection → **starter strip** (shingles with tabs removed, or reversed shingles, or type M roll roofing) projecting ≥ 12 mm (½ in.) beyond eaves, rakes and fascia (drip edge; metal drip edges also ok), nailed 300 mm o.c. → first course with butt edge in line with bottom of starter strip → subsequent courses at allowed exposure (depends on slope, shingle type/length), aligned with chalk lines or underlay print lines.
- **Four large-head roofing nails per strip**, penetrating ≥ 12 mm into sheathing. Self-sealing tar seals. Fig. 101 labels: roof sheathing, eave protection, roofing nail, tar seals, exposure, fascia board, starting course.

#### Asphalt shingles on low slopes 1:6 to 1:3
- Three thicknesses everywhere except first two courses, incl. hips and ridges; **exposure ≤ ⅓ shingle height**. Starter strips over a continuous cement band ≥ 200 mm (8 in.) wide; first course cemented with a band exposure + 100 mm (e.g. 250 mm for 150 mm exposure); subsequent courses band exposure + 50 mm (200 mm for 150 mm exposure); band 25–50 mm above butt edge to avoid defacing. Four fasteners above exposed portion. Cold cement ≈ 0.5 L/m², hot ≈ 1 kg/m². Only needed below 1:4 — special low-slope shingles keep three thicknesses at ≥ 1:4.

#### Wood shingles (**Fig. 102**)
- Western red / white cedar heartwood (decay-resistant, low shrinkage), No. 1 and No. 2 grades; width **75–350 mm (3–14 in.)**; other species preservative-treated. Underlay/felt not usually required; eave protection required.
- First course **doubled**, upper overlapping joints, both rows projecting ~**25 mm (1 in.) beyond fascia** (figure: 12 mm / ½ in. for drip). **6 mm (¼ in.) gap** between shingles; joints offset **≥ 40 mm** from joints in course below and not aligned with the two previous courses.
- **Two nails per shingle**, at exposure + 40 mm from butt (e.g. 125 mm exposure → nail at 165 mm), **20 mm edge distance**; hot-dip galvanized/corrosion-resistant. Flat-grain shingles > 200 mm wide may be split and nailed as two.
- Fig. 102 labels: eave protection ≥ 300 mm beyond inside face of wall, roof sheathing, two nails per shingle, 20 mm edge distance, wood shingles, exposure, 40 mm lap, 6 mm space, fascia board, first course (double), project shingles 12 mm for drip.

#### Shakes (**Fig. 103**)
- Cedar hand-split: **length ≥ 450 mm (18 in.), width 100–350 mm (4–13¾ in.), butt 9–32 mm (⅜–1¼ in.)**. Min pitch **1:3**.
- Over spaced or closed sheathing; spaced: 19 × 89 mm (1 × 4) or wider strips on centres = exposure, never > 250 mm (10 in.); closed recommended where wind-driven snow.
- Exposure **190 mm (7½ in.) for 450 mm shakes, 250 mm (10 in.) for 600 mm (24 in.) shakes**.
- 900 mm (36 in.) No. 15 felt at eave line; starter course doubled (tripled for texture), bottom course 380 or 450 mm shakes. After each course, 450 mm (18 in.) No. 15 felt strip over top portion, bottom edge at **2 × exposure above butts** (e.g. 600 mm shakes @ 250 mm → felt 500 mm above butts, covering top 100 mm of shakes and ~350 mm onto sheathing). Gap **6–9 mm**; side joints offset ≥ 40 mm; froe-end (smoother) uppermost.

#### Finish at ridge and hips (**Fig. 104**)
- Asphalt: shingle squares (⅓ strip) over ridge/hip, blind-nailed, lapped to same coverage; orient cap away from prevailing wind. Wood: 150 mm (6 in.) wide shingles alternately lapped and blind-nailed, over No. 15 felt; flashing sometimes under wood ridge.

#### Built-up roofs (**Fig. 105**)
- Specialist installers; ≥ 3 layers of felt each sealed with tar or asphalt; gravel or cap sheet as ballast/UV protection. Coal tar and asphalt products incompatible.
- Eave trimmed with metal edging/flashing; gravel stop or cant strip with flashing. At walls: mopped to cant strip, turned up ≥ 150 mm (6 in.), sheathing paper and siding lapped over (50 mm min lap). Masonry-clad wall: membrane turned up, flashing over, counter-flashing embedded ≥ 25 mm in mortar, down ~150 mm, lapping ≥ 100 mm. Single-ply membranes also usable. Fig. 105 labels: siding, sheathing membrane, 50 mm minimum lap, membrane flashing, cant strip, roof sheathing, built-up roofing, metal gravel stop, fascia board.

#### Sheet metal roofing (**Fig. 106**)
- Widths **762–914 mm (30–36 in.)**, any length. Min slope **1:4** unless manufacturer proves lower. Over spaced supports: sheets designed for snow load, support under each end joint. Min thickness: 0.33 mm galvanized steel, 0.46 mm copper/zinc, 0.48 mm aluminum. Fig. 106 accessories: nailing strips for sheet metal roofing, eave starter, ridge cap, end wall flashing, valley, cottage hip, side wall flashing.

#### Concrete and clay tile roofing
- Considerably heavier; roof structure engineered for the additional load.

### Sustainable housing insight — Ch. 12 (p. 147)
- Deflect all water away from roof and walls; drip edges beyond materials below.
- Orient roof for future solar; finish service life ≥ renewable system; stiffer sheathing/closer framing for panels; building-integrated PV tiles.
- Make roof surface dimensions **multiples of 400 or 600 mm (16 or 24 in.)** to reduce panel waste; metal recyclable; wood renewable; keep roofs clear of leaves/branches to dry; concrete tile durable but heavy — extra framing/seismic reinforcement.

## Summary for procedural modelling — hip roof framing sequence

Members and rules for generating a site-framed hip roof (Figs. 82, 83B, 85, 87, 97–99):

1. **Walls:** double top plates on exterior walls; studs/plates define the rectangular footprint. Optional interior load-bearing wall along the centre.
2. **Ceiling joists:** span the short direction at 400 or 600 mm o.c. (305/406/610 mm to suit panels), nailed to plates **before rafters**; lapped over the centre bearing wall. Typical 38 × 140 mm (2 × 6) for ~4.3 m span @ 400 mm. Near hip ends where the hip rafter leaves no room, use a **doubled joist** set inboard plus **stub/tail joists** to the end plate at the same spacing (Fig. 85).
3. **Ridge board:** level, centred on the short span; length = building length − building width (for equal-pitch hips, hip rafters meet the ridge ends at 45° in plan). Slope < 1:3 requires a ridge beam (38 × 140 mm) on 38 × 89 mm struts at 1.2 m, or a bearing wall.
4. **Common rafters:** from plates to ridge board in opposite pairs (or offset ≤ one thickness), bird's-mouth at the plate, heel bearing directly over the wall; depth ≥ 300 mm at wall face if insulation requires; spacing = joist spacing. Typical 38 × 184 mm @ 300 mm or 38 × 235 mm @ 600 mm for a 4.7 m span at 1:3 (Ottawa snow). Ceiling joist nailed to the side of each rafter.
5. **Hip rafters:** four, from each building corner to the ridge ends, at 45° in plan; **depth = common rafter depth + 50 mm (2 in.)**.
6. **Jack rafters:** from plates to hip rafters (hip jacks) on both the long and short sides, spacing continuing the common-rafter module, progressively shorter toward the corner, nailed to hip and plate.
7. **Valleys (L-plans):** valley rafter (also +50 mm deep) from the inside corner to the ridge; valley jacks from ridge to valley.
8. **Intermediate support if needed:** collar ties 38 × 89 mm on rafter pairs (slope ≥ 1:3), struts ≥ 45°, dwarf walls (slope < 1:3), strongback (2 × 38 × 89 mm) under hip-end jacks.
9. **Eaves/overhangs:** rafter tails project past the wall; fascia at rafter ends; soffit with perforated vent; gable-end overhangs (gable roofs only) via rake rafter (< 300 mm) or lookouts 600 mm o.c. (> 300 mm).
10. **Sheathing:** 1220 × 2440 mm panels, long dimension (face grain) perpendicular to rafters, staggered joints, 2–3 mm gaps, H-clips on unsupported edges, nails 150 mm edge / 300 mm field; trimmed tight at hips and valleys. Or 19 mm boards ≤ 286 mm wide, closed (edge to edge, joints staggered over supports) or spaced at the shingle exposure for wood shingles/shakes; diagonal in high wind/seismic areas.
11. **Covering:** eave protection 900 mm up slope; starter course; asphalt shingles (exposure 130/145 mm, ≥ 1:3) or wood shingles (exposure ~125 mm, ≥ 1:4) or shakes (exposure 190/250 mm, ≥ 1:3); ridge and hip caps lapped away from prevailing wind.
12. **Ventilation:** soffit intake + ridge/gable exhaust, ≥ 1/300 of ceiling area, 63 mm (or 25 mm with baffles) clear above insulation at eaves.

# Headless renderer for the Fable run of experiment 13.
#
# Usage:
#   blender --background --python render_fable.py -- <experiment.py> <lib_dir> <out_prefix> [view,view,...]
#
# Renders Workbench (solid) views with object outlines on, so coplanar boards
# stay distinguishable. Collections can be hidden per view for visibility.

import bpy
import sys
import os
import math
from mathutils import Vector

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
experiment_path, lib_dir, out_prefix = argv[0], argv[1], argv[2]
only_views = set(argv[3].split(",")) if len(argv) > 3 else None

sys.path.insert(0, lib_dir)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(experiment_path)))

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
exec(compile(open(experiment_path).read(), experiment_path, "exec"), {"__name__": "__main__"})

scene = bpy.context.scene


def bounds(objs):
    pts = [o.matrix_world @ Vector(c) for o in objs for c in o.bound_box]
    lo = Vector((min(p.x for p in pts), min(p.y for p in pts), min(p.z for p in pts)))
    hi = Vector((max(p.x for p in pts), max(p.y for p in pts), max(p.z for p in pts)))
    return (lo + hi) / 2, max((hi - lo).length / 2, 0.001)


meshes = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"]
if not meshes:
    print("No mesh objects generated, aborting render.")
    sys.exit(1)
full_center, full_radius = bounds(meshes)

# --- Per-collection object colours (Workbench OBJECT colour mode) ---
COLORS = {
    "Timber_Framing": (0.62, 0.42, 0.24, 1.0),
    "Sheathing": (0.90, 0.80, 0.55, 1.0),
}


def colorize(coll, color):
    color = COLORS.get(coll.name, color)
    for o in coll.objects:
        o.color = color
    for c in coll.children:
        colorize(c, color)


for c in scene.collection.children:
    colorize(c, (0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 1.0))

# --- Render settings ---
scene.render.engine = "BLENDER_WORKBENCH"
sh = scene.display.shading
sh.light = "STUDIO"
sh.color_type = "OBJECT"
sh.show_cavity = True
sh.cavity_type = "BOTH"
sh.show_object_outline = True
sh.object_outline_color = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
sh.show_shadows = False
scene.render.resolution_x = 1600
scene.render.resolution_y = 1200
scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("World")
scene.world.color = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)

cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new("HeadlessCam")
cam_data.type = "ORTHO"
cam_data.clip_start = 0.01
cam_data.clip_end = full_radius * 40
cam = bpy.data.objects.new("HeadlessCam", cam_data)
scene.collection.objects.link(cam)
scene.camera = cam

aspect = min(scene.render.resolution_x, scene.render.resolution_y) / \
         max(scene.render.resolution_x, scene.render.resolution_y)


def all_collections(coll):
    yield coll
    for c in coll.children:
        yield from all_collections(c)


# View spec: azimuth/elevation in degrees, collections to hide, optional focus
# (center, radius) for close-ups.
VIEWS = [
    dict(name="01", azim=60, elev=30, hide=[]),
    dict(name="02", azim=150, elev=30, hide=[]),
    dict(name="03", azim=240, elev=30, hide=[]),
    dict(name="04", azim=330, elev=30, hide=[]),
    dict(name="05", azim=90, elev=89.0, hide=[]),
    dict(name="06", azim=60, elev=30, hide=["Sheathing"]),
    dict(name="07", azim=75, elev=25, hide=[], focus=(Vector((0.0, 2.2, 1.0)), 4.8)),
    dict(name="08", azim=250, elev=35, hide=[], focus=(Vector((0.0, -4.5, 1.0)), 5.5)),
    dict(name="09", azim=75, elev=25, hide=["Sheathing"], focus=(Vector((0.0, 2.2, 1.0)), 4.8)),
    dict(name="10", azim=120, elev=30, hide=[], focus=(Vector((0.0, 2.0, 1.5)), 2.6)),
    dict(name="11", azim=300, elev=40, hide=[], focus=(Vector((3.0, -4.0, 1.0)), 2.6)),
    dict(name="12", azim=30, elev=30, hide=[], focus=(Vector((4.5, 0.0, 2.0)), 2.6)),
]

for view in VIEWS:
    if only_views and view["name"] not in only_views:
        continue
    for coll in all_collections(scene.collection):
        coll.hide_render = coll.name in view["hide"]

    center, radius = view.get("focus", (full_center, full_radius))

    azim = math.radians(view["azim"])
    elev = math.radians(view["elev"])
    offset = Vector((

# --- Overlap check: every member is a convex polyhedron (box or prism),
# so test pairs with the separating-axis theorem over face normals and
# edge cross products and report the minimum penetration depth. ---
def hull(o):
    M = o.matrix_world
    verts = [M @ v.co for v in o.data.vertices]
    R = M.to_3x3()
    normals = []
    for p in o.data.polygons:
        n = (R @ p.normal).normalized()
        if not any(abs(abs(n.dot(m)) - 1) < 1e-6 for m in normals):
            normals.append(n)
    edges = []
    for e in o.data.edges:
        d = (verts[e.vertices[1]] - verts[e.vertices[0]]).normalized()
        if not any(abs(abs(d.dot(m)) - 1) < 1e-6 for m in edges):
            edges.append(d)
    lo = Vector((min(v.x for v in verts), min(v.y for v in verts), min(v.z for v in verts)))
    hi = Vector((max(v.x for v in verts), max(v.y for v in verts), max(v.z for v in verts)))
    return verts, normals, edges, lo, hi


def penetration(a, b):
    va, na, ea, _, _ = a
    vb, nb, eb, _, _ = b
    axes = na + nb + [x.cross(y) for x in ea for y in eb]
    depth = float("inf")
    for ax in axes:
        if ax.length < 1e-9:
            continue
        ax = ax.normalized()
        pa = [v.dot(ax) for v in va]
        pb = [v.dot(ax) for v in vb]
        gap = max(min(pa) - max(pb), min(pb) - max(pa))
        if gap >= 0:
            return 0.0
        depth = min(depth, -gap)
    return depth


hulls = [(o.name, hull(o)) for o in meshes]
TOL = 0.001

    if any(a[3][i] > b[4][i] - TOL or b[3][i] > a[4][i] - TOL for i in range(3)):
        continue
    p = penetration(a, b)
    if p > TOL:
        hits.append((p, name_a, name_b))
hits.sort(reverse=True)
print(f"OVERLAP CHECK: {len(hulls)} members, {len(hits)} penetrating pairs (> {TOL * 1000:.0f} mm)")
for p, name_a, name_b in hits:

# --- Overlap check: every member is a convex polyhedron (box or prism),

# edge cross products and report the minimum penetration depth. ---
def hull(o):
    M = o.matrix_world
    verts = [M @ v.co for v in o.data.vertices]
    R = M.to_3x3()
    normals = []
    for p in o.data.polygons:
        n = (R @ p.normal).normalized()
        if not any(abs(abs(n.dot(m)) - 1) < 1e-6 for m in normals):

    edges = []
    for e in o.data.edges:

        if not any(abs(abs(d.dot(m)) - 1) < 1e-6 for m in edges):

# CRAFT BOT - Experiment 08 (Fable run) - Segal Method two-storey house
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Post-and-beam timber frame house after Walter Segal's method (AJ special
# issue, 5 Nov 1986, J. Broome), following the building sequence of the
# source: foundations (10) -> structural frame (11) -> roof (12) ->
# floors (13) -> external walls (14) -> windows (15) -> stairs (18).
#
#   * tartan grid: 600 panel + 50 structural band = 0.65 m module
#   * structural bay 6 modules = 3.9 m post to post (3.85 m clear)
#   * cross-frames along Y at x = 0, 3.9, 7.8, 11.7, 14.3 (last = patio
#     frame); post lines y = 0, 3.9, 7.8; house 11.7 x 7.85 m + 2.6 m
#     covered patio on the east, all under one 15 deg pitched roof
#   * posts 50 x 150 on pad foundations, beams 50 x 200 bolted to both
#     post faces, joists 50 x 200 at every band on 50 x 50 bearers
#     (notched ends so undersides are flush, fig 50/51)
#   * double-height void over bay 2 south half, stair on its north edge
#   * infill walls: 12 ply / 50 core / 12 ply clamped between 50 x 25
#     battens on the bands; site-made glazing with mullions on the bands
#
# Coordinates: X = along the house (west -> east), Y = across (south ->
# north), Z up, ground at z = 0.  Units: metres.  Axis-aligned members
# are craftbot.place_element boxes; sloped members are convex prisms.

import math

Y_RIDGE = 3.925                              # centre of the middle band

OVERHANG_X = 0.60                            # beyond outer roof beam faces
SLAB = BEAM_D / math.cos(PITCH)              # vertical depth of roof slab
BEARER_V = BEARER / math.cos(PITCH)
DECK_T = 0.018 / math.cos(PITCH)
KERB_H = 0.15
GLASS = 0.006
POST_OUT = 0.10                              # post projection outside core

def get_collection(path):
    parent = bpy.context.scene.collection
    for name in path.split("/"):
        child = parent.children.get(name)
        if child is None:

            if child is None:

            parent.children.link(child)
        parent = child

    for c in obj.users_collection:

    get_collection(coll).objects.link(obj)
    return obj


def box(name, coll, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1):

        name=name,
        loc=((x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2, (z0 + z1) / 2),

    p, n = Vector(p), Vector(n)

    out = []

    return zu(y) + SLAB

    """Plumb-cut parallelogram (y, z) profile between two roof-parallel
    height functions (must not straddle the ridge)."""
    return [(y0, lo(y0)), (y1, lo(y1)), (y1, hi(y1)), (y0, hi(y0))]


def roof_piece(name, coll, x0, x1, y0, y1, lo, hi):
    """A piece straddling the ridge is split plumb at the ridge into two

    if y0 < Y_RIDGE - 1e-6 and y1 > Y_RIDGE + 1e-6:

post_xy = [(x, y) for x in FRAMES_X for y in POST_Y]

    box(f"Pad_{i:02d}", "Foundation", x - PAD / 2, x + PAD / 2, yc - PAD / 2, yc + PAD / 2, -PAD_DEPTH, 0.0)

## 0. About this document (template)

This file is the template for future experiment runs
(`experiment_NN_<model>_design_rationale.md`). Sections and their purpose:

| § | Section | Purpose |
|---|---------|---------|
| 0 | About this document | Template note (this table). |
| 1 | How to run / outputs | Exact command, view legend, file naming, collections — enough to regenerate everything. |
| 2 | Reading the inputs | Which manual figures/pages were used and how they became numbers and rules; where the model deliberately deviated from the source. |
| 3 | Reading the reference code | Key dimensions and conventions inherited from earlier scripts; mistakes made while reading them. |
| 4 | Why the frame/model had to change | Problems found in the inherited model that blocked the task, and the fix chosen vs. alternatives. |
| 5 | Core modelling decisions | The few decisions that made the result possible (representation, algorithms), with rejected options. |
| 6 | Detailed geometry | Derivations, edge cases, evolution across versions and why each earlier variant was dropped. |
| 7 | Verification | Visual and numeric checks, their false positives, what was *not* verified. |
| 8 | Iterations | One row per saved version: change → what the renders/checks showed. |
| 9 | Scope and known simplifications | What was deliberately left out or approximated. |

Sections can be added, merged or renamed as the experiment demands (e.g. a
"Parameter study" or "Structural check" section); keep the numbering and the
"what vs. why, including rejected options" spirit. Write the rationale at the
end of the run while the reasoning is still in context, then archive the
session transcript last.

## 1. How to run / outputs

Every iteration `experiment_13_fable_vNN.py` was executed in background
Blender 4.3 by `render_fable.py` (Workbench, object outlines on so coplanar
boards stay distinguishable), producing `*_blender_view_NN.png` and a `.blend`.
Run from this folder:

```
blender -b --python render_fable.py -- experiment_13_fable_v04.py ../input <abs_out_prefix> [01,05,...]
```

Views: 01–04 orbit, 05 top, 06 framing only, 07/09 dormers (with/without
boards), 08 south wing, 10 dormer close-up, 11 wing valley, 12 east hip apex.
v01 has views 01–09 only (10–12 were added from v02).

Construction rules applied (CMHC Fig. 98, closed method): 19 × 184 mm boards
edge to edge, parallel to the eaves on every facet, last row ripped at the
ridge; every joint over a rafter (0.6 m main grid, 0.4 m dormer grid), 3.6 m
stock, odd rows start with a half board; mitred ends at hips, valleys, ridges.
Collections: `Timber_Framing/{Main_Roof,South_Wing,Dormers}` and
`Sheathing/{Main_Roof,South_Wing,Dormers}`. Final model: v04, 622 boards.

## 2. Reading the inputs

- `wood_board_roof_sheating.png` (CMHC Fig. 98) and
  `canadian_wood_frame_roof_extracted.md` §Lumber boards: closed method = boards
  edge to edge, ends supported, joints staggered; 19 mm thick; ≤ 286 mm wide;
  boards ≤ 184 mm take two nails per bearing → chose 184 mm (8 in. nominal) as
  the board width: it is the widest "two-nail" board and gives a readable
  number of rows. Boards run perpendicular to the rafters, i.e. parallel to the
  eaves, on every facet including hip triangles (the previous ChatGPT run had
  boards running up-slope on the E/W hips, which contradicts Fig. 98).
- Fig. 88 (dormers): sheathing is installed first, dormer framed on top,
  sheathing cut flush around the opening. I followed the "cut flush around the
  framing" rule for the main-roof cutout but did **not** add the bottom plate on
  the sheathing because the v18 frame stands its studs directly on the rafters;
  changing that would be a frame redesign, outside the sheathing scope.
- Fig. 99: sheathing fitted tightly at hips and valleys and nailed to the
  hip/valley rafter → boards must end *on* the hip/valley line with bevelled
  ends, not short of it.

## 3. Reading the reference code (v18 frame – key numbers that drove decisions)

Main roof 18 × 9 m, slope 1:2, plate z = 0, ridge z = 2.25, rafters 38 × 184 at
0.6 m. Wing 6 × 6 m, ridge z = 1.5, valley top at (0, −1.5, 1.5). Dormers:
`half_w = (stud_width + 2·1.5·spacing)/2 = 0.94`, overhang 0.2 → eave at
ox ± 1.14, 35° pitch, top plate z = 1.22, ridge z = 2.018, header at y = 0.46.

Important: I initially mis-estimated the dormer half-width as 0.49 m (forgot the
`2 · support_half` term) and designed the first cutout on that basis → v01's
self-intersecting cutout. Lesson recorded: derive dormer dimensions with the
same function the frame uses (`dormer_geom` replicates
`build_dormer_on_north_slope`) rather than by hand.

Member orientation conventions needed for the protrusion math:
`create_prismatic_member` puts width on local X (horizontal, across the member),
depth on local Y (perpendicular to the member in the slope plane), length on Z;
`rafter_between` puts length on X, width on Y, depth on Z. The generic
protrusion formula Σᵢ eᵢ·|aᵢ·n| over the three scaled local axes avoids caring
about which convention a member used.

## 4. Why the frame had to be corrected before sheathing

The user asked only for sheathing, but "no geometric inconsistencies" is
impossible on the v18 frame as-is:

- **Hips are deeper than commons** (184 + 50 mm) and centred on the plane
  intersection, so their top edge sits ≈ 111 mm above the centre-plane versus
  92 mm for the rafter tops: they would pierce the boards by ~25 mm. Wing hips
  and valleys (1.25 × depth) pierce by ~24 mm. Standard carpentry fix is
  "dropping the hip" (lower the seat cut); I implemented that as a translation
  along the member's own depth axis, computed per member from the adjacent
  facets, rather than hand-tuning numbers. Alternative rejected: thin the hip
  section to 181 mm — hides the issue instead of modelling the real detail.
- **Dormer valley rafters** in v18 run from `(x_left, back_y)` to the header,
  which lies in the main plane but *not* in the dormer roof plane (130 mm off at
  the foot), so the dormer valley jacks would poke out of the dormer boards.
  Rebuilt on the true plane intersection, extended to seat on the doubled
  rafter at `x_left` (foot ends up at y ≈ 1.72 instead of 2.1). Everything
  depending on that line (jacks, braces, trimmed commons) was regenerated by
  name — `craftbot.place_element` deletes a same-named object, so re-creating
  by name is a clean way to override single members without copying 1200 lines
  of v18.
- **Dormer valleys vs dormer boards**: the dormer rafters are only 80 mm deep,
  so the 184 mm valley (main-rafter section) is 59 mm proud of the dormer
  sheathing underside → dropped 59 mm (it is then also 50 mm under the main
  boards, which is fine; jacks still land on it).
- **Square-edged ridge boards** have corners above the two sloped undersides
  (dormer ridge 11 mm, main/wing ridge 1 mm) → same drop pass.
- Collar ties and side top plates grazed boards by millimetres → trimmed.

## 5. Core modelling decisions

### 5.1 Boards are polygon meshes, not scaled cubes

The ChatGPT approach (one scaled cube per row) gives square ends. At a hip the
square ends of two facets' boards either overlap or leave a sawtooth gap,
because the hip line is diagonal in each board's frame. A board that is cut on
site has a bevelled (mitred) end. Modelling that requires a prism whose top and
bottom outlines differ → built directly with `bpy.data.meshes.new` from two
2D outlines. This is the single decision that made "no interpenetration, no
gaps" achievable.

### 5.2 Facet/outline model and the offset-plane trick

Every facet is described by origin O, eave direction U, up-slope V, normal N,
and the underside offset (half rafter depth). Outline vertices are never typed
in; each is the intersection of three planes (`isect`): two roof planes (hip,
valley, ridge) or a roof plane and vertical boundary planes (eave lines,
dormer eave x = const, front beam y = const). Doing this at two offset levels
("underside" and "top") means a shared edge between facets A and B is
A(h)∩B(h) for both facets at both levels → the two boards share one end face.

Evolution, with the reason each earlier variant was rejected:

1. **v01/v02 – clip at the centre-plane line (offset 0) for convex edges, at the
   top-surface line for concave edges.** Reasoning: centre-plane clipping at a
   convex edge leaves a V-gap but never overlaps; top-surface clipping at a
   concave edge (valley, dormer junction) makes tops meet and the end faces
   diverge downward. Worked, but the V-gap at hips/ridge is see-through once the
   hip is dropped (visible in v02 views 11/12), and the dormer ridge/junction
   apex did not lie on both lines, giving a slightly skewed top board.
2. **v03 – two outlines per board (underside + top).** Removes both problems and
   also makes the dormer apex consistent because three planes at one level meet
   at a single point that is on both of its edges.

Valley vs hip asymmetry considered: with symmetric offsets the top-surface
intersection is directly above the centre-line intersection for both, so the
same code handles hips, valleys and ridges. For the dormer/main junction the
offsets differ (40 vs 92 mm underside) so the junction line shifts ≈ 75 mm
toward the dormer ridge at the foot; the main boards therefore cantilever a few
cm past the valley rafter centre — within "fit tightly at valleys" tolerance and
preferable to a hole.

## 6. Detailed geometry

### 6.1 Main-roof cutout around a dormer (three attempts)

- Attempt A (design notes only): rectangle between doubled rafters + triangle
  where the dormer roof is above the main roof. Abandoned on paper because it
  would leave a void between the triangle base and the plate end and cut boards
  unsupported next to the studs.
- Attempt B (v01): heptagon rect ∪ triangle. Self-intersected because the
  dormer eave (±1.14) is outside the doubled rafters (±0.9 + stud half-width).
- Attempt C (v02+): pentagon = two eave lines + front beam face + two junction
  lines up to the apex. The dormer roof covers everything inside; the main
  boards run under the overhang up to the eave line. Side top plates were
  shortened to start where the main sheathing top passes under them (y ≈ 2.35)
  so the plate's back end does not sit inside a board.

### 6.2 Row layout, joints, stagger

- Rows start at the eave with full 184 mm boards; the ridge row is ripped
  (slivers < 40 mm merged into the previous row, as a carpenter would).
- Joint positions = rafter lines projected to the facet's u axis; a board run is
  cut at the farthest rafter within 3.6 m of its start; odd rows start with a
  1.8 m board → joints stagger and always fall on a rafter. Rafter grids: main
  x = −8.7…8.7 step 0.6 (commons + jacks happen to share one grid), E/W y = 0.6k,
  wing y = −4.5 − 0.6i and x = −3 + 0.6k, dormers y = 3.7 − 0.4i.
- Scan-line construction: a row strip is intersected with the outline (even-odd
  over outer + hole loops) at its bottom and top edge; matching interval counts
  give trapezoids with exactly bevelled ends. Where an outline vertex falls
  inside a row (valley apex, dormer apex, eave-back corner) the row is split
  into bands at those v values so each band is again trapezoidal. Alternative
  rejected: general polygon clipping with holes (a lot of code for three
  vertices), or decomposing facets into convex pieces (would create joints at
  arbitrary lines, not on rafters). The only remaining approximation is a
  ≈ 1 cm band at valley apexes where the underside and top vertex v differ and
  square ends are used.

## 7. Verification

- Visual: 12 fixed views incl. framing-only and close-ups; outlines on so
  coplanar boards are distinguishable; per-view bounding-box camera fit (the
  bounding-sphere fit from `tools/run_experiment_headless.py` left the model at
  ~40 % of the frame).
- Numeric: `report_protrusions` — for every framing member, if its bounding-box
  corners straddle a facet's underside and a corner lies inside the sheathed
  region (point-in-polygon, even-odd), report the excess. First version flagged
  dormer rafter tails that are entirely *above* the main boards (true positives
  of the test, false positives for the question), fixed by requiring the member
  to straddle the underside. v04: 0 hits.
- Not verified numerically: board-vs-board overlap. Argued by construction
  (shared planes/lines); a BVH overlap test would report touching faces too and
  was not worth the noise.

## 8. Iterations

| v | change | result |
|---|--------|--------|
| 01 | first full implementation | boards OK; dormer cutout self-intersecting (dormer eave overhangs the doubled rafters), collar ties graze dormer boards, bounding-sphere camera wastes frame |
| 02 | cutout = eave lines + front beam + valley lines; collar ties trimmed; per-view camera fit | clean layout; thin see-through gap along hips/ridge because boards were clipped at the rafter centre-planes |
| 03 | two-level outlines → mitred board ends; exact valley-apex rows | hips/valleys/ridge closed; dormer ridge board top corners 7 mm into boards |
| 04 | ridge boards included in the drop pass | 0 protrusions, 622 boards, final |

## 9. Scope and known simplifications

Rafter tails square-cut; no fascia/soffit; dormer wall bottom plate; ventilation
details; nailing. `tools/run_experiment_headless.py` untouched (a run-specific
renderer was added instead of changing the shared tool).
Frame numbers: hips dropped 28 mm (main) / 26 mm (wing hips, valleys),
dormer valleys 59 mm, dormer ridges 11 mm, main and wing ridge 1 mm. The ≈ 1 cm
band at each valley apex uses square instead of mitred ends.

  (slivers < 40 mm merged into the previous row, as a carpenter would).
- Joint positions = rafter lines projected to the facet's u axis; a board run is
  cut at the farthest rafter within 3.6 m of its start; odd rows start with a
  1.8 m board → joints stagger and always fall on a rafter. Rafter grids: main
  x = −8.7…8.7 step 0.6 (commons + jacks happen to share one grid), E/W y = 0.6k,
  wing y = −4.5 − 0.6i and x = −3 + 0.6k, dormers y = 3.7 − 0.4i.
- Scan-line construction: a row strip is intersected with the outline (even-odd
  over outer + hole loops) at its bottom and top edge; matching interval counts
  give trapezoids with exactly bevelled ends. Where an outline vertex falls
  inside a row (valley apex, dormer apex, eave-back corner) the row is split
  into bands at those v values so each band is again trapezoidal. Alternative
  rejected: general polygon clipping with holes (a lot of code for three
  vertices), or decomposing facets into convex pieces (would create joints at
  arbitrary lines, not on rafters). The only remaining approximation is a
  ≈ 1 cm band at valley apexes where the underside and top vertex v differ and
  square ends are used.

## 7. Verification

- Visual: 12 fixed views incl. framing-only and close-ups; outlines on so
  coplanar boards are distinguishable; per-view bounding-box camera fit (the
  bounding-sphere fit from `tools/run_experiment_headless.py` left the model at
  ~40 % of the frame).
- Numeric: `report_protrusions` — for every framing member, if its bounding-box
  corners straddle a facet's underside and a corner lies inside the sheathed
  region (point-in-polygon, even-odd), report the excess. First version flagged
  dormer rafter tails that are entirely *above* the main boards (true positives
  of the test, false positives for the question), fixed by requiring the member
  to straddle the underside. v04: 0 hits.
- Not verified numerically: board-vs-board overlap. Argued by construction
  (shared planes/lines); a BVH overlap test would report touching faces too and
  was not worth the noise.

## 8. Iterations

| v | change | result |
|---|--------|--------|
| 01 | first full implementation | boards OK; dormer cutout self-intersecting (dormer eave overhangs the doubled rafters), collar ties graze dormer boards, bounding-sphere camera wastes frame |
| 02 | cutout = eave lines + front beam + valley lines; collar ties trimmed; per-view camera fit | clean layout; thin see-through gap along hips/ridge because boards were clipped at the rafter centre-planes |
| 03 | two-level outlines → mitred board ends; exact valley-apex rows | hips/valleys/ridge closed; dormer ridge board top corners 7 mm into boards |
| 04 | ridge boards included in the drop pass | 0 protrusions, 622 boards, final |

Rafter tails square-cut; no fascia/soffit; dormer wall bottom plate; ventilation
details; nailing. `tools/run_experiment_headless.py` untouched (a run-specific
renderer was added instead of changing the shared tool).
Frame numbers: hips dropped 28 mm (main) / 26 mm (wing hips, valleys),
dormer valleys 59 mm, dormer ridges 11 mm, main and wing ridge 1 mm. The ≈ 1 cm
band at each valley apex uses square instead of mitred ends.

def place_element(name, loc=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
                  angle=0.0, scale=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
    """
    Create (or replace) a cube called `name` and place it in the scene
    with a transform defined by loc / axis / angle / scale.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Blender object name. Existing object with this name will be replaced.
    loc : 3-tuple or Vector
        World-space location of the object (translation).
    axis : 3-tuple or Vector
        Rotation axis in world space.
    angle : float
        Rotation angle in degrees.
    scale : 3-tuple or Vector
        Per-axis scale factors.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Coerce parameters to Vectors

    loc_vec = Vector(loc)
    axis_vec = Vector(axis)
    if axis_vec.length == 0:
        axis_vec = Vector((0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
    else:
        axis_vec.normalize()

    scale_vec = Vector(scale)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cube geometry in local space (size 2×2×2 centered at origin)

    verts = [
        Vector(( 1.0,  1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0, -1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0, -1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0,  1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0,  1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0, -1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0, -1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0,  1.0,  1.0)),
    ]

    faces = [
        (0, 1, 2, 3),
        (4, 7, 6, 5),
        (0, 4, 5, 1),
        (1, 5, 6, 2),
        (2, 6, 7, 3),
        (4, 0, 3, 7),
    ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Create mesh and object

    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    mesh.from_pydata(verts, [], faces)
    mesh.update()

    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh)
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(obj)

    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    obj.select_set(True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Build TRS matrix and assign once

    angle_rad = math.radians(angle)

    S = Matrix.Diagonal((scale_vec.x, scale_vec.y, scale_vec.z, 1.0))
    R = Matrix.Rotation(angle_rad, 4, axis_vec)
    T = Matrix.Translation(loc_vec)

    obj.matrix_world = T @ R @ S

class Frame:
    """Plane through o spanned by orthonormal u, v; n = u x v."""

    def __init__(self, o, u, v):
        self.o, self.u, self.v = Vector(o), Vector(u).normalized(), Vector(v).normalized()
        self.n = self.u.cross(self.v).normalized()

    def to2d(self, q):
        d = Vector(q) - self.o
        return (d.dot(self.u), d.dot(self.v))

    def clip(self, poly, p, n):
        """Clip by the 3D half-space (q - p) . n >= 0 restricted to the plane."""
        p, n = Vector(p), Vector(n)
        return clip_lin(poly, (self.o - p).dot(n), self.u.dot(n), self.v.dot(n))

    def point(self, a, b, t=0.0):
        return self.o + self.u * a + self.v * b + self.n * t


def slab_coeffs(fr, p, n, t0, t1):
    """Line coefficients (c, ca, cb) in `fr` such that the WHOLE slab
    (extruded t0..t1 along fr.n) satisfies (q - p) . n >= 0 where
    c + ca*a + cb*b >= 0: the plane is shifted by the worst-case thickness
    term, so thick members never pierce it."""
    p, n = Vector(p), Vector(n)
    dn = fr.n.dot(n)
    return (fr.o - p).dot(n) + min(t0 * dn, t1 * dn), fr.u.dot(n), fr.v.dot(n)


def slab_clip(fr, pts, p, n, t0, t1):
    return clip_lin(pts, *slab_coeffs(fr, p, n, t0, t1))


def frame_prism(name, coll, fr, pts, t0, t1, clips=()):
    """Convex prism: polygon `pts` in `fr`, extruded along fr.n from t0 to
    t1, after clipping by 3D half-spaces [(p, n)] (exact for the full
    thickness).  None if clipped away."""
    for p, n in clips:
        pts = slab_clip(fr, pts, p, n, t0, t1)
        if len(pts) < 3:
            return None
    lo = [fr.point(a, b, t0) for a, b in pts]
    hi = [fr.point(a, b, t1) for a, b in pts]
    return mesh_prism(name, coll, lo, hi)

    """Convex polygon minus a convex hole given as inside half-spaces
    [(p, n, clearance)]; returns a list of convex pieces, each fully
    outside the hole over the slab thickness t0..t1."""
    pieces, rest = [], pts
    for p, n, cl in holes:
        p = Vector(p) - Vector(n) * cl

        outside = clip_lin(rest, c, ca, cb)
        if len(outside) >= 3:

        rest = clip_lin(rest, -c, -ca, -cb)          # exact complement: pieces never overlap

    return clip_lin(pts, *slab_coeffs(fr, p, n, t0, t1))


def frame_prism(name, coll, fr, pts, t0, t1, clips=()):
    """Convex prism: polygon `pts` in `fr`, extruded along fr.n from t0 to
    t1, after clipping by 3D half-spaces [(p, n)] (exact for the full
    thickness).  None if clipped away."""
    for p, n in clips:
        pts = slab_clip(fr, pts, p, n, t0, t1)
        if len(pts) < 3:
            return None

    hi = [fr.point(a, b, t1) for a, b in pts]
    return mesh_prism(name, coll, lo, hi)


def subtract(fr, pts, holes, t0=0.0, t1=0.0):
    """Convex polygon minus a convex hole given as inside half-spaces
    [(p, n, clearance)]; returns a list of convex pieces, each fully
    outside the hole over the slab thickness t0..t1."""
    pieces, rest = [], pts
    for p, n, cl in holes:
        p = Vector(p) - Vector(n) * cl
        c, ca, cb = slab_coeffs(fr, p, -Vector(n), t0, t1)
        outside = clip_lin(rest, c, ca, cb)
        if len(outside) >= 3:
            pieces.append(outside)
        rest = clip_lin(rest, -c, -ca, -cb)          # exact complement: pieces never overlap
        if len(rest) < 3:
            break
    return pieces

    p, q = Vector(p), Vector(q)
    d = (q - p).normalized()
    n = Vector((-d.y, d.x))
    a, b = p - d * ext, q + d * ext
    h = width / 2
    return [tuple(a - n * h), tuple(b - n * h), tuple(b + n * h), tuple(a + n * h)]


def positions(a0, a1, spacing, thick, grid0=None):
    if grid0 is None:

    first, last = a0 + thick / 2, a1 - thick / 2
    pos = [first]
    k = math.ceil((first + spacing / 2 - grid0) / spacing - 1e-9)
    p = grid0 + k * spacing
    while p < last - spacing / 2:
        pos.append(p)
        p += spacing
    pos.append(last)
    return pos

def row_pieces(loops_u, loops_t, v0, v1, eps=1e-5):
    """
    Exact (underside, top) outline pairs covering the row v0..v1. The row is
    split into bands at every polygon vertex inside it so that every band is
    bounded by straight edges only and can be described by trapezoids.
    """
    inner = sorted(set(v for loops in (loops_u, loops_t) for loop in loops
                       for (_, v) in loop if v0 + 2 * eps < v < v1 - 2 * eps))
    bands = [v0] + inner + [v1]
    pairs = []

            continue
        lo_t, hi_t = scan_intervals(loops_t, b0 + eps), scan_intervals(loops_t, b1 - eps)
        lo_u, hi_u = scan_intervals(loops_u, b0 + eps), scan_intervals(loops_u, b1 - eps)
        if len(lo_t) != len(hi_t):

def drop_member(name, facets):
    """

    DROP_CLEARANCE under the sheathing underside of every adjacent facet
    ("dropping the hip"). Returns the applied drop.
    """
    obj = bpy.data.objects.get(name)
    if obj is None:
        return 0.0
    M = obj.matrix_world
    axes = [M.col[i].xyz for i in range(3)]
    drop = 0.0
    for facet in facets:
        n = facet.N
        protrusion = sum(abs(a.dot(n)) for a in axes)
        excess = protrusion - facet.underside + DROP_CLEARANCE
        if excess <= 0.0:

        if depth_axis.dot(n) < 0.0:

                stud_width, stud_depth, plate_thickness, rafter_width,
                rafter_depth, overhang, rafter_spacing):
    """Replicates the derived dimensions of base.build_dormer_on_north_slope."""
    half_W = main_geom["half_W"]
    ridge_height = main_geom["ridge_height"]
    plate_z = main_geom["plate_z"]
    main_spacing = main_geom["rafter_spacing"]
    main_tan = (ridge_height - plate_z) / half_W

    support_half = 1.5 * main_spacing
    width = stud_width + 2.0 * support_half
    half_w = width * 0.5
    top_plate_z = wall_height + plate_thickness * 0.5
    m = math.tan(math.radians(roof_pitch_deg))
    run = half_w + overhang
    ridge_z = top_plate_z + run * m
    y_ridge_back = -(ridge_z - ridge_height) / main_tan
    front_y = oy
    back_y = oy - depth

    num_rafters = max(3, int(depth / rafter_spacing) + 2)
    rafter_ys = [front_y - min(i * rafter_spacing, depth) for i in range(num_rafters)]

    return dict(
        ox=ox, front_y=front_y, back_y=back_y, depth=depth,
        x_left=ox - support_half, x_right=ox + support_half,
        half_w=half_w, run=run, ridge_z=ridge_z, top_plate_z=top_plate_z,
        y_ridge_back=y_ridge_back, stud_width=stud_width, stud_depth=stud_depth,
        plate_thickness=plate_thickness, rafter_width=rafter_width,

def collar_half_len(dg, facet, z_top, margin=0.01):

    """
    Re-create the dormer members that depend on the valley line so that the
    valley rafters lie exactly on the intersection of the dormer roof plane and
    the main roof plane, seated on the doubled rafters at x_left / x_right.
    """
    ox = dg["ox"]
    ridge_z = dg["ridge_z"]
    y_rb = dg["y_ridge_back"]
    ridge_height = main_geom["ridge_height"]
    raf_w, raf_d = main_geom["rafter_size"]

    N0 = facet_N.plane(0.0)
    valley_top = Vector((ox, y_rb, ridge_z))
    feet = {}
    for side, facet, x_seat in (("L", facet_L, dg["x_left"]), ("R", facet_R, dg["x_right"])):
        foot = isect(facet.plane(0.0), N0, vplane("x", x_seat))
        feet[side] = foot
        base.rafter_between(
            name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_Valley_{side}",
            E=foot, R=valley_top, section_y=raf_w, section_z=raf_d,
        )

        # valley jacks + their top braces, feet on the corrected valley line
        n_jacks = 3
        for j in range(n_jacks):
            t = (j + 1) / (n_jacks + 1.0)
            y_j = foot.y + t * (y_rb - foot.y)
            P_valley = foot.lerp(valley_top, (y_j - foot.y) / (valley_top.y - foot.y))
            base.rafter_between(
                name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_Valley_Jack_{side}_{j}",
                E=P_valley, R=Vector((ox, y_j, ridge_z)),
                section_y=dg["rafter_width"], section_z=dg["rafter_depth"],
            )
            if side == "R":
                P_L = feet["L"].lerp(valley_top, (y_j - feet["L"].y) / (valley_top.y - feet["L"].y))
                z_b = P_L.z + 0.6 * (ridge_z - P_L.z)
                half_len = min(abs(P_valley.x - P_L.x) * 0.24,
                               collar_half_len(dg, facet_L, z_b + dg["plate_thickness"] * 0.5))
                base.box(
                    name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_ValleyTopBrace_{j}",
                    center=(ox, y_j - dg["stud_depth"], z_b),
                    size=(2.0 * half_len, dg["stud_depth"], dg["plate_thickness"]),
                )

    # collar ties between the dormer rafters, trimmed clear of the boards
    z_b = ridge_z - (ridge_z - dg["top_plate_z"]) * 0.3
    half_len = min(0.225 * (2.0 * dg["half_w"] - 2.0 * dg["stud_width"]),
                   collar_half_len(dg, facet_L, z_b + dg["plate_thickness"] * 0.5))
    for i, y_pos in enumerate(dg["rafter_ys"]):
        brace_y = max(min(y_pos - dg["stud_depth"], dg["front_y"]), y_rb)
        base.box(
            name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_TopBrace_{i}",
            center=(ox, brace_y, z_b),
            size=(2.0 * half_len, dg["stud_depth"], dg["plate_thickness"]),
        )

    # trimmed main rafters: ridge -> corrected valley
    spacing = main_geom["rafter_spacing"]
    ridge_half = main_geom["ridge_half"]
    grid = [-ridge_half + i * spacing for i in range(int(main_geom["ridge_len"] / spacing) + 1)]
    interior = [x for x in grid if dg["x_left"] < x < dg["x_right"]]
    for idx, x_r in enumerate(interior):
        foot = feet["L"] if x_r < ox else feet["R"]
        t = (x_r - foot.x) / (valley_top.x - foot.x)
        P_valley = foot.lerp(valley_top, t)
        base.create_prismatic_member(
            name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_TrimmedTop_{idx}",
            start=Vector((x_r, 0.0, ridge_height)), end=P_valley,
            width=raf_w, depth=raf_d,
        )

    # side top plates: start where the main sheathing top passes under them
    z_plate_bottom = dg["top_plate_z"] - dg["plate_thickness"] * 0.5
    z_top_at_ridge = ridge_height + facet_N.top / facet_N.N.z
    y_clear = (z_top_at_ridge - z_plate_bottom) / dg["main_tan"]
    y_back = max(dg["back_y"], y_clear)
    for i, x_val in enumerate((dg["x_left"], dg["x_right"])):
        base.box(
            name=f"D{d_id}_Dormer_TopPlate_Side_{i}",
            center=(x_val, 0.5 * (dg["front_y"] + y_back), dg["top_plate_z"]),
            size=(dg["stud_width"], dg["front_y"] - y_back, dg["plate_thickness"]),
        )

def point_in_loops(u, v, loops):
    inside = False
    for loop in loops:
        n = len(loop)
        for i in range(n):
            u0, v0 = loop[i]
            u1, v1 = loop[(i + 1) % n]
            if (v0 <= v < v1) or (v1 <= v < v0):
                if u < u0 + (v - v0) / (v1 - v0) * (u1 - u0):
                    inside = not inside
    return inside

    """Print every framing member whose corner pokes through a sheathed area."""
    hits = []
    for name in frame_names:
        obj = bpy.data.objects.get(name)
        if obj is None:
            continue
        corners = [obj.matrix_world @ Vector(c) for c in obj.bound_box]
        for facet, loops in facet_regions:
            heights = [(P - facet.O).dot(facet.N) for P in corners]
            if min(heights) > facet.underside:
                continue          # entirely above the boards (e.g. dormer rafter tails)
            worst = 0.0
            for P, h in zip(corners, heights):
                if h > facet.underside + tol:
                    u, v = facet.uv(P)
                    if point_in_loops(u, v, loops):
                        worst = max(worst, h - facet.underside)
            if worst > 0.0:
                hits.append((name, facet.name, worst))
    print(f"[check] framing members poking through sheathing: {len(hits)}")
    for name, fname, h in sorted(hits, key=lambda x: -x[2]):
        print(f"[check]   {name:40s} {fname:10s} +{h * 1000:.1f} mm")
    return hits

            ca, cb = fr.u.dot(n), fr.v.dot(n)
            base, dn = (fr.o - p).dot(n), fr.n.dot(n)
            lo = clip_lin(lo, base + min(t0 * dn, t1 * dn), ca, cb)
            if len(lo) < 3:
                return None, []
        hi = lo
    obj = mesh_prism(name, coll, [fr.point(a, b, t0) for a, b in lo],
                     [fr.point(a, b, t1) for a, b in hi])
    return obj, lo


def member(name, coll, p0, d, m, ztop, depth, width, s0, s1, clips=()):
    """Straight member in the vertical plane through p0 (x, y) along the
    horizontal unit direction d. Top line z = ztop + m*s (s = horizontal
    distance from p0), depth measured perpendicular to the top line,
    width across the plane, plumb ends at s0 and s1 before clipping."""
    d = Vector((d[0], d[1], 0.0)).normalized()
    fr = Frame((p0[0], p0[1], 0.0), d, (0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
    dv = depth * math.sqrt(1.0 + m * m)
    pts = [(s0, ztop + m * s0 - dv), (s1, ztop + m * s1 - dv),
           (s1, ztop + m * s1), (s0, ztop + m * s0)]
    return frame_prism(name, coll, fr, pts, -width / 2, width / 2, clips)


def hs(p, n):
    return (Vector(p), Vector(n).normalized())


def vx(x, sign):
    return hs((x, 0.0, 0.0), (sign, 0.0, 0.0))


def vy(y, sign):
    return hs((0.0, y, 0.0), (0.0, sign, 0.0))


def vz(z, sign):
    return hs((0.0, 0.0, z), (0.0, 0.0, sign))


PLATE_TOP = vz(Z_PL, 1.0)


def cheek(C, d, toward):
    """Vertical side face of a 38 mm member whose centre line passes
    through C along d, on the side of point `toward`."""
    d = Vector((d[0], d[1], 0.0)).normalized()
    lat = Vector((-d.y, d.x, 0.0))
    if (Vector((toward[0], toward[1], 0.0)) - Vector((C[0], C[1], 0.0))).dot(lat) < 0:
        lat = -lat
    return hs(Vector((C[0], C[1], 0.0)) + lat * (T / 2), lat)


class Roof:
    """Roof plane z = z0 + s*(c - out.q); `out` = outward horizontal
    direction of the facet, so the plane rises inward."""

    def __init__(self, name, out, c, z0=Z_T0, s=S):
        self.name = name
        self.out = Vector((out[0], out[1], 0.0)).normalized()
        self.c, self.z0, self.s = c, z0, s
        self.n = Vector((s * self.out.x, s * self.out.y, 1.0)).normalized()
        self.p = Vector((self.out.x * c, self.out.y * c, z0))

    def z(self, x, y):
        return self.z0 + self.s * (self.c - (self.out.x * x + self.out.y * y))

    def below(self, off=0.0):
        return (self.p + self.n * off, -self.n)

    def above(self, off=0.0):
        return (self.p + self.n * off, self.n)


class Facet:
    """One roof facet: wall-line origin O (a = 0), eave direction A,
    inward direction Sd, rafter grid (a values), body clips (ridge face,
    hip / valley cheeks) and the eave plane for the tails."""

    def __init__(self, name, roof, O, A, Sd, grid, clips, coll, run=MAIN_Y):
        self.name, self.roof, self.coll, self.run = name, roof, coll, run
        self.O = Vector((O[0], O[1], 0.0))
        self.A = Vector((A[0], A[1], 0.0)).normalized()
        self.Sd = Vector((Sd[0], Sd[1], 0.0)).normalized()
        self.grid = list(grid)
        self.clips = list(clips)
        self.eave = hs(self.O - self.Sd * OV, self.Sd)
        self.skip = set()

    def pt(self, a, s):
        return self.O + self.A * a + self.Sd * s


def rafter(fac, a, name, extra=(), tail=True, depth=RAF_D):
    """Common / jack rafter of facet `fac` at eave position a. The body
    is cut by the facet clips (ridge, hips, valleys) and seated on the
    plate; a tail is added when the body still reaches the wall line."""
    p0 = fac.pt(a, 0.0)
    clips = fac.clips + list(extra) + [PLATE_TOP]
    obj, poly = member(name, fac.coll, p0, fac.Sd, S, Z_T0, depth, T, 0.0, fac.run + 1.0, clips)
    if obj is not None and tail and min(s for s, _ in poly) < 1e-4:
        member(name + "_tail", fac.coll, p0, fac.Sd, S, Z_T0, depth, T, -OV - 0.3, 0.0, [fac.eave])
    return obj


def hip_member(name, coll, C, d, body_clips, tail_clips, drop=HIP_DROP):
    ztop = Z_T0 - drop
    member(name, coll, C, d, HIP_M, ztop, HIP_D, T, 0.0, 12.0, list(body_clips) + [PLATE_TOP])
    member(name + "_tail", coll, C, d, HIP_M, ztop, HIP_D, T, -OV * R2 - 0.3, 0.0, list(tail_clips))


def wall(tag, coll, x0, x1, y0, y1):
    """Stud wall: bottom plate, studs @ 600 from the start + end stud,
    double top plate. Long axis picked from the extents."""
    along_x = (x1 - x0) > (y1 - y0)
    a0, a1 = (x0, x1) if along_x else (y0, y1)
    box(f"{tag}_BottomPlate", coll, x0, x1, y0, y1, 0.0, T)
    box(f"{tag}_TopPlate_1", coll, x0, x1, y0, y1, Z_PL - 2 * T, Z_PL - T)
    box(f"{tag}_TopPlate_2", coll, x0, x1, y0, y1, Z_PL - T, Z_PL)
    pos = [a0 + T / 2]
    k = 1
    while a0 + k * SP < a1 - T - 0.1:

        else:
